ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • 4-day history of very severe headache after returning from Thailand (multiple mosquito bites).  
  • Subjective fever developed after headache onset.  
  • Diffuse, red, itchy, blanching rash appeared “all over body.”  
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Day 0: headache began.  
  • Day 1-2: feverish sensation, feeling cold.  
  • Day 3-4: generalized myalgias; rash noticed.  
  • No improvement with paracetamol or ibuprofen.  
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat tightness/closing: none reported.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: none.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: none.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: none.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: none.  
  • Swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): none.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: denies earache.  
  • Neck pain/stiffness: denies neck stiffness; admits generalized aches only.  
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar episodes; no hospitalizations or injection therapy.  
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food allergies: none known.  
  • Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented); no regular medications.  
- Social context:
  • Video consultation from secure location; no mention of accompaniment.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: none described.  
- Airway/breathing: no stridor, no respiratory distress reported.  
- Mental status: alert, conversant.  
- Vitals: Not recorded.  
- Physical examination findings: limited to patient-reported blanching rash.  
- Third person present: none stated.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: Febrile illness with severe headache and blanching pruritic rash after recent travel to Thailand; high suspicion for mosquito-borne arboviral infection (dengue most likely). Meningitis considered but less likely on history; requires exclusion with physical exam ± labs.  
- Evidence: Travel <1 week ago, mosquito exposure, fever, severe headache, myalgias, blanching rash, no photophobia/neck stiffness, rash blanches.  
- Differential diagnosis (aligned with DDx):
  1. Dengue fever – high likelihood: classic triad (fever, severe headache, myalgias) plus blanching rash 3–5 days after onset; recent Thailand travel.  
  2. Chikungunya virus – moderate likelihood: similar vector and symptoms; less joint pain reported.  
  3. Malaria – moderate likelihood: fever/headache post-Thailand; rash atypical but disease serious enough to exclude.  
  (Meningitis considered; opposing evidence: no neck stiffness, photophobia, or non-blanching rash.)  
- No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.

Plan:
- Urgent in-person evaluation recommended within hours for full physical exam, vitals, and labs (CBC, platelets, LFTs, malaria screen, dengue serology, blood cultures).  
- Advise patient to attend designated clinic hub today; if unavailable, proceed directly to hospital ED.  
- Red-flag instructions: seek immediate care if severe neck stiffness, altered consciousness, photophobia, worsening headache, persistent fever, rash becomes non-blanching, bleeding, breathing difficulty, or vomiting develop.  
- Symptomatic relief: may continue paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed, adhering to maximum daily doses.  
- No ENT-specific treatment required at present; monitor for any airway or oropharyngeal swelling though unlikely given current presentation.  
- Follow-up: arrange review of test results and possible infectious-disease referral; reinforce mosquito-bite prevention for future travel.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: documented temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, full ENT and neurological exam, medication dosages, vaccination history, malaria prophylaxis history.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; occasional minor fillers but content intelligible.
